known.title: Step gate_wiring adds a third gate-run case of plan-skill-phases.mjs to scripts/ci.mjs but no Files cell lists scripts/config/test-contracts.json, whose pinned selector and expected_min the test-contract registry check compares against the gate's invocations, so the full gate fails.
known.locator: Steps, row 5 gate_wiring, Task and Files (line 87); Research, Verdict text, separate-case paragraph (line 61); Acceptance A10 (line 103)
known.summary: Evidence at repo_ref: scripts/tests/test-contracts.mjs gateInvocationArguments() and gateSelection() (lines 208-239) parse every node()/nodeOk() call of scripts/ci.mjs and build the selector of a suite with several cases by joining the sorted case values with '|'; line 366 asserts that the registry selector equals that descriptor, and lines 367-371 check expected_min. scripts/config/test-contracts.json entry repo-plan-skill-phases (lines 137-155) pins the selector 'scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs --case bounded-workflows|plan-workspace-template' and expected_min 2 (lines 147-148). scripts/AGENTS.md lines 130-142 document this rule. scripts/ci.mjs runs test-contracts.mjs in the repo-wide guards (lines 299-301). Scenario: step gate_wiring adds nodeOk(['scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs', '--case', 'review-verdicts']) to the plan orchestration section. The discovered selector becomes '... --case bounded-workflows|plan-workspace-template|review-verdicts' with 3 invocations, the registry still says the two-case selector, so test-contracts.mjs fails with 'repo-plan-skill-phases selector differs from gate descriptor' and Acceptance A10 (node scripts/ci.mjs exits 0) cannot pass; no step or Files cell names the registry. Fix: add scripts/config/test-contracts.json to the Files of step gate_wiring, set the selector to 'scripts/tests/plan-skill-phases.mjs --case bounded-workflows|plan-workspace-template|review-verdicts' and expected_min to 3, and add an Acceptance row for node scripts/tests/test-contracts.mjs.

known.title: Research item 2 claims that both wrappers cap Performance findings at MEDIUM, but they cap Performance at HIGH, so the advisory-caps sentence that step wrapper_verdicts writes lets a HIGH Performance finding ride on a pass.
known.locator: Research, Consumers of the verdict semantics, item 2 (line 20); Research, Verdict text, advisory caps (line 45) and its justification (line 52); Steps, row 1 wrapper_verdicts, Task (line 83)
known.summary: Evidence at repo_ref: plugins/plan-lifecycle/agents/code-reviewer.md line 51 says 'Performance severity never exceeds `HIGH`' (the MEDIUM cap at line 57 applies only to Maintainability); .codex/agents/code-reviewer.toml line 24 and plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-workspace/references/codex-agent-templates.md line 56 say the same. The plan claims both buckets cap at MEDIUM (line 20), concludes that the bucket rule and the severity rule agree (line 52), and step wrapper_verdicts writes 'Maintainability and Performance findings stay advisory under their caps and never force fixes-required' into all three wrapper files (lines 45, 83). Scenario: a reviewer finds a hot-path N+1 query and rates it HIGH Performance, as the wrapper allows. The advisory-caps sentence tells it the finding never forces fixes-required, while the fixes-required sentence and the record rule say that any HIGH forces it and that a code-review pass has no HIGH line. A reviewer that follows the bucket sentence returns 'Code-review: pass' with an open HIGH line; plan.mjs line 898 then accepts that pass at archive, which breaks the Goal's split between advisory MEDIUM/LOW rounds and blocking CRITICAL/HIGH findings. Fix: correct item 2 (Performance caps at HIGH, only Maintainability caps at MEDIUM) and limit the advisory-caps sentence to Maintainability, or drop it and let severity alone decide the verdict.

The repeated-HIGH case of the request still blocks, the Goal states the same bound, steps manager_phase6 and contract_sync carry it, and Acceptance A3/A4 check it; no instruction file or contract rule at repo_ref requires more rounds.
